Priyanka: Thanks for joining the infra Q&A follow-up. Dropping the answers people asked for on procurement, pre-warming, and autoscaler safety nets.
Dev: Short summary: APAC pilot still on for late-May but exact regions shifted due to rack availability. Primary will be KUL with SYD as sibling; SIN is delayed.
Noah: Procurement note: partnership paperwork delayed a week; we chose KUL because immediate spares available + cheaper spot inventory for burst. Customers on low-latency SLAs will be notified.
Sasha: Q: How does the autoscaler choose between reserved vs burst vs sibling region? Can we get the exact decision tree?
Dev: Decision tree (brief): 1) Reserved pool in requested region (if customer's reservation exists), 2) Burst pool in region (shared spot), 3) Pre-warmed standby nodes (if policy allows), 4) Sibling APAC region, 5) EU fallback, 6) US-west final fallback. We'll publish a visual in the follow-up doc.
Priyanka: Q from legal/compliance: how do we enforce data residency when we hit capacity issues?
Sasha: API flag sample below; when `residency: "strict"` we will never cross-region and will return 429 + header `x-rdi-reason: residency_block` when capacity unavailable. If `residency: "preferred"` we follow the decision tree above.
Dev: Sample route snippet: ```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"ap-southeast-3","residency":"strict"}
```
Noah: Q: What happens if a spot-backed burst VM evicts during an active inference?
Sasha: Flow: graceful drain window ~18s -> snapshot KV-cache -> if eviction abrupt, request returns 502 + `x-rdi-trace` and autoscaler issues a single backend retry to the next fallback path for idempotent calls. We'll add recommended client retry guidance.
Priyanka: Q: Cold-start SLAs for APAC? We need numbers for customers.
Dev: Targets: node provision <= 110s in KUL (quota-constrained), model warm-up medians: 7B ~ 18-25s, 13B ~ 30-45s, 70B ~ 60-85s. We'll publish median + p95 in Console telemetry.
Noah: Any new protective measures for Dedicated customers during big PLG spikes?
Sasha: Yes 1: autoscaler v1.2 includes a cross-tenant circuit-breaker that trims burst allocation if global token-rate > threshold for X minutes. Affected requests will see `x-rdi-circuit: active` header and org-level alerts. Dedicated reservations are never evicted.
Priyanka: Billing concerns: will customers be charged for cross-region egress if we failover?
Dev: No surprise bills. Cross-region failover requires an org-level opt-in `allow_cross_region_fallback`. Console will show projected egress estimates before enabling and we'll emit alerts when cross-region spend exceeds configurable thresholds.
Noah: Ops request: can SRE add a short tag for traces so Support can quickly find residency-related failures?
Sasha: Yes 1: We'll add `residency_mode`, `region`, and `model_variant` tags on cold-start and eviction traces. Support will get a console view with trace ids.
release-bot: Starting canary: autoscaler v1.2 -> 5% traffic (ETA ~4m).
Priyanka: Action items: (1) Dev to publish decision-tree diagram + sample configs by EOD, (2) Sasha to add headers & telemetry tags PR by Thu, (3) Console to mock opt-in + egress estimate UI next sprint, (4) Docs to write 1-paragraph FAQ "spot eviction" + SDK sample for `residency` flag.
release-bot: Canary passed -> autoscaler v1.2 at 5% healthy.
Noah: Thanks team. I'll coordinate the customer comms and post the consolidated follow-up doc in #product-update before EOD. Ping me for urgent edits.
